reason: Same article, same medium and same variable: series 535841-s1 is the TEM geometric-diameter particle-count mean of Au nanoparticles ablated from a 99.99% gold rod in pure 18 MOhm deionized water (medium_class water, no additives) at 800 nm, 110 fs, 1 kHz, over five fluences 60, 160, 539.5, 795.8 and 1000 J/cm2. That is exactly the variable, material, medium and range of the claim's own evidence (the text states the mean size dropped from 120 to 4 nm as F decreased from 1000 to 60 J/cm2), and the series endpoints (4.07 nm at 60 J/cm2, 124.85 nm at 1000 J/cm2) reproduce the text's values, so the pair is comparable on the stated terms without any proxy.
caveats: Mixed size_source: the 60, 160 and 1000 J/cm2 points are histogram means computed from stored bar centres with particles_counted = 1000 and sd_over_sqrt_n errors, while the 539.5 and 795.8 J/cm2 points are scalar means with no stored SD or N, so their errors are the 10%/20% size fallbacks. Endpoint values differ slightly from the text (4.07 vs 4 nm, 124.85 vs 120 nm) because of histogram binning. At intermediate fluences the text resolves two Gaussian components (narrow and broad distributions, Fig. 2) and reports component means, whereas these series points are whole-distribution means, so the intermediate points do not correspond to the text's component-resolved values; the claim itself is about the whole mean size. Five points test only the monotone direction, not the two-mechanism interpretation, the bimodality or any saturation.
